title: Skin, hair and nails
examples: What are the different layers of skin?
Why do we sweat when it is hot?
What does melanin do for our skin?

explain.say: The skin is actually made of several different layers.
The epidermis is the very top layer of your skin.
Sweating helps to cool your body down when you get too hot.
Melanin is a natural pigment that gives skin its colour.
Our nails and hair are also covered by skin and are made of tough proteins.

draw.text: Nails and hair: Made of keratin

explain.say: When you play outside in the hot sun, your skin uses melanin for protection.

faq.q: Why do I get freckles sometimes?
faq.a: Freckles are often areas where your skin produces more melanin. This is a natural reaction to sun exposure. You might also ask: What causes dark spots on skin? Or: Why do some people have more freckles?

faq.q: Does skin get damaged if I burn it?
faq.a: A bad sunburn damages the outer layers of your skin. It can make you more sensitive to the sun next time. Other ways to ask: What happens after a sunburn? Or: How do I care for burned skin?
asks: What is the best way to prevent burns?

faq.q: Is sweat just water, or does it have other things in it?
faq.a: Sweat is mostly water, but it also contains salts and some other minerals. When it evaporates, it takes heat away from your body. You could also ask: What is sweat made of? Or: Does sweat taste salty?
asks: What is the purpose of sweating?
How does sweat cool me down?

faq.q: Are nails and hair made of the same material?
faq.a: Yes, both nails and hair are primarily made of a tough protein called keratin. This protein gives them strength and structure. You might also ask: What is keratin? Or: What are nails and hair made from?
asks: What is the building block of nails?
Do hair and nails share a material?

faq.q: Does the skin protect me from germs?
faq.a: Yes, the skin acts as a physical barrier against many germs and dirt. It is the body's first line of defence. Other questions include: How does skin stop germs? Or: Is skin waterproof?

facts: Skin is the largest organ in the human body.
The outer layer of skin is called the epidermis.
Sweat cools the body through evaporation.
Melanin is the pigment that determines skin colour.

quiz.say: Which layer is the outermost protective layer of the skin?
quiz.why: The epidermis is correctly named as the very top layer of the skin.

wrong.0: The hypodermis is the fatty layer found beneath the skin structure.
wrong.1: Keratin is a protein found in nails, not a skin layer itself.
wrong.3: The dermis is the layer underneath the epidermis, not the outermost one.

quiz.say: When you are too hot, what process helps cool your body?
quiz.why: Sweat cools you because the water in it changes from liquid to gas.

wrong.0: Melanin deals with colour and sun protection, not cooling the body.
wrong.1: Thickening the skin does not help remove excess body heat.
wrong.2: Nail growth is related to protection, not temperature control.

quiz.say: If you spend time in strong sunlight, what substance increases to protect your skin?
quiz.why: Melanin is the pigment that increases to provide natural sun protection.

wrong.0: Keratin is a protein found in nails and hair, not a sun shield.
wrong.1: The dermis is a layer, but melanin is the specific protective pigment.
wrong.3: Sweat helps cool you down, but it does not block UV rays.
